Lessons.Title: Divide with Partial Quotients
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will introduce you to ways to record partial quotients when dividing multi-digit numbers.
Previously, you have found quotients by decomposing a dividend and finding the quotient for each decomposed part until all of the dividend is divided. You have also reasoned in terms of multiplication—adding partial products until you reach the value of the dividend—and in terms of place value. You have also used area diagrams and base-ten diagrams—among other representations—to support your reasoning.
Source activity sequence: Warm-up: Number Talk: Divide by 3 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Decompose Dividends (20 minutes); Activity 2: Tyler’s Method (15 minutes); Cool-down: Subtract Groups (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Record each convenient portion of a dividend as a partial quotient; add the quotient contributions.
Edulytics authored model: 465 = 400 + 60 + 5. Divide the parts by 5: 80 + 12 + 1 = 93. Verify 5 × 93 = 465.
First-party Cool-down: Use partial quotients to find 684 ÷ 6.
